Executive Summary
Introduction
This document outlines the High-Level Design (HLD) for the 
BSE
 application, providing an overview of its architecture and design for DEFRA
.
 
T
he
 BSE system manages suspected and confirmed positive BSE cases under Active and Passive Surveillance workflows. It supports 
RBSE
 (
Risk
Based Surveillance for BSE
)
 allocation, case data entry across multiple tabs, lab result updates, and stores scanned documents in SharePoint. The system also provides search, reporting, and audit logging to maintain compliance and traceability.
Background
DEFRA seeks to exit from Civica-managed hosting and support arrangements by migrating and modernising 
five
 critical Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) applications to secure, compliant, and sustainable Defra Cloud-based platforms. These legacy applications are currently distributed across Civica, Atos Datacentre, and hybrid configurations, and require remediation, rationalisation, and alignment with Defra’s cloud-first strategy and security standards. 
We wish to undertake a project to move the solution towards alignment of the technologies and practices of the Defra Cloud Centre of Excellence (CCoE) definitions, demonstrating benefits against observed obsolescence, technical debt and security markers, without widespread implementation and significant business disruption.
The proposed solution will be planned to deliver benefits against observed obsolescence, technical debt and security markers, without widespread implementation leading to significant business disruption
.
Document 
Purpose
The purpose of this High-level Design
 
is to define the cloud-migration approach for delivering cloud-native solution within the Defra Azure tenancy. This design aligns with the Cloud Centre of Excellence (CCoE) patterns and standards, and incorporates Defra’s security principles to ensure a secure, compliant and robust architecture. Cut down extra complexity by using one standard set of components and stopping the use of old platforms and services that cost money to license and maintain.
It also provides a clear foundation for delivering the same functionality capability currently in use, while positioning the service for future scalability and enhancement opportunities
.
 The design ensure that existing service levels and resilience expectations and operational standards are preserved and improved, with any business functional and non-functional gaps highlighted for further refinement in subsequent low-level design work.
Business Stakeholders – 
To provide sufficient information for business stakeholders to understand the design.
Architecture, Data, Information, and Innovation teams (ADII)
 – As part of the governance review cycle and to provide traceability of architectural governance.
DEFRA Suppliers and Partners
 – To provide sufficient information for completion of delivery estimation and detailed design, and subsequent design Integrity review for completeness and consistency.
Audience
The intended audience for this document includes: 
Solution architects
, who examine the overall architecture, validating patterns such as Hub-Spoke, security measures, and integration approaches to confirm compliance with enterprise architecture standards. 
Cloud architects
 and the 
infrastructure team
, who reviews network configurations, security controls, and Azure resource designs, ensuring proper implementation of VNet peering, private endpoints, and firewall setups. 
Security and compliance team
, who validates identity models, firewall configurations, NSGs, and Key Vault usage, ensuring adherence to organizational and regulatory standards.
Application development team
, who assesses the hosting model such as App Service along with authentication mechanisms like Entra ID and integration points, planning any necessary code changes or migration steps. 
Data engineering team
, who evaluates data flows and database migration strategies, focusing on performance and security for data synchronization. 
Business stakeholders
, including product owners and business users, who focus on ensuring the design support key business processes and aligns with organisational goals.
Operations and support team
, who reviews the operational readiness including monitoring, logging, backup, and disaster recovery strategies to prepare for a smooth handover.
Project management and governance teams
, who tracks dependencies, timelines, and risks, ensuring alignment with the cloud adoption framework, governance policies, retention, and audit requirements. Key project stakeholders include APHA, Civica, and DDTS teams
.
Scope
The scope includes designing the Azure architecture and landing zone required to host applications in Azure. 
This design will cover four environments
 
DEV, QA, 
PreProd
, and Production
 
within the primary Azure region (UK South). Additionally, the use of Azure Infrastructure as Code (IaC) through Bicep templates
. T
he 
BSE
 application will be deployed to Azure as a greenfield implementation
 and 
this application within the Azure landing zone, utilising both Azure IaaS and PaaS capabilities. Azure DevOps will be used to enable Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) for delivering the application onto the Azure platform
.
In Scope
The following items define the activities and components that will be included as part of the migration and implementation effort.
 
Migration Approach
Migration will involve refactoring all 
BSE
 application components to Azure to ensure minimal disruption, with only minimal code changes to ensure compatibility with Azure hosting requirements. 
The UI and functionality will remain unchanged. Additionally, 
BSE
 database will be migrated to Azure SQL, using Azure SQL Database for improved scalability and performance
.
Application Hosting
The
 BSE web application 
will be deployed 
on Azure App Service
,
 
running within a dedicated App Service Plan to provide a scalable, fully managed hosting environment. Secure access to the application is enforced through integration with CCoE managed Application Gateway and its Web Application Firewall (WAF)
.
Identity &amp; Access
Legacy
 Windows Authentication 
will be replaced 
with 
Microsoft 
Entra ID (
formerly 
Azure AD) 
to enable modern, cloud-based 
user authentication.
 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) will be implemented across Azure resources to ensure least-privilege 
of 
access and secure resource management.
Networking
A Hub-and-Spoke network architecture will be implemented to provide centralized connectivity and security controls. Private endpoints will be configured for critical services such as SQL databases, App Service, and Key Vault to prevent exposure to the public internet.
Data Integration
Data synchronization
 from TSE to BSE 
will be scheduled and automated 
using Azure Data Factory (ADF) pipelines.
 All data transfers will be secured through private endpoints to maintain compliance and reduce the risk of data breaches.
Security &amp; Compliance
Security will be strengthened through the use of Azure Firewall, Network Security Groups (NSGs), Private DNS zones, and Azure Key Vault for managing sensitive information. Microsoft Sentinel and Log Analytics will be enabled to provide advanced monitoring, threat detection, and compliance reporting.
Monitoring &amp; Logging
Azure 
monitor will check the infrastructure, Logic Monitor and 
Application Insights will
 monitor
 the
 BSE web application. Centralized logging and alerting will be implemented across all components to streamline troubleshooting and operational oversight.
Governance
The Cloud Centre of Excellence (CCoE) enforces security standards through centrally managed Azure Policy, and existing CCoE cost-management strategy will be adopted. A cost management strategy, supported by resource tagging, will be adopted to ensure effective budget tracking and accountability
.
Remediation
Obsolescence Reduction
The to
be architecture removes reliance on outdated, end
of
life technologies and platforms by migrating the BSE application to 
cloud
native Azure PaaS services
.
Legacy platforms retired
: Windows Server 2016, IIS 10, and unsupported ASP.NET Web Forms (.NET 4.0) are decommissioned.
Modern runtime alignment
: The application is upgraded to 
.NET Framework 4.8.x
, which is supported, secure, and aligned with Defra’s approved technology stack.
Managed platform adoption
: Application hosting moves to 
Azure App Service
, eliminating dependency on manually managed servers and OS patching.
Database modernisation
: On
premises SQL Server is replaced with 
Azure SQL Database
, removing hardware and platform lifecycle risks.
Standards alignment
: The solution aligns with Defra Cloud Centre of Excellence (CCoE) patterns, ensuring long
term supportability.
Limited refactor
:
 
the solution will be 
updated only 
where necessary 
for remediation
 purposes
 through 
library/runtime uplift, security fixes, config changes
 
while ensuring that 
feature and 
functional parity with the as-is application is preserved
.
 
Technical Debt Reduction
The to
be design addresses accumulated technical debt by simplifying architecture, standardising tooling, and automating operational processes.
Removal of manual processes
: Manual IIS deployments, server maintenance, and ad
hoc configuration are replaced with 
automated CI/CD pipelines
 using Azure DevOps.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
: Environment provisioning and configuration are managed using 
Bicep
, ensuring consistency, repeatability, and auditability.
Environment separation
: Dedicated 
Dev, Test, UAT, and Production
 environments remove the risk of testing in production.
Platform efficiencies
: PaaS services handle patching, scaling, backups, and resilience, reducing operational overhead.
Simplified architecture
: Fragmented infrastructure and over
engineering are reduced in favour of a unified, cloud
native design.
Security Strengthening
Security is embedded throughout the to
be architecture using a 
secure
by
design and zero
trust approach
, fully aligned with Defra security standards.
Identity and access control
: 
Authentication and authorization via 
Azure Entra ID
.
Role
based access control (RBAC), MFA, and Conditional Access applied.
Network security
: 
Hub
and
spoke architecture
 with centralized ingress and egress control.
Azure Firewall, Web Application Firewall (WAF), NSGs, and Private DNS used to govern traffic.
Private Endpoints
 ensure databases and services are not exposed to the public internet.
Data protection
: 
Encryption at rest
 using Azure SQL Transparent Data Encryption (TDE).
Encryption in transit
 enforced with TLS 1.2+ for all connections.
Secrets and credentials stored securely in 
Azure Key Vault
, removing plaintext credentials from code.
Monitoring and threat detection
: 
Azure Monitor, Application Insights, and Log Analytics
 provide centralized observability.
Microsoft Sentinel and Defender for SQL
 enable security monitoring, auditing, and threat detection.
Secure access for analytics
: 
Read
only database access with strict isolation and auditing controls.
Secure storage of s
ecrets 
with controlled 
access 
using
 managed identities
Out of Scope
The following items represent activities and enhancements that are excluded from the current migration phase and will not be addressed at this time.
Application Code Refactoring
The 
BSE
 application is planned for migration to 
.NET Framework 4.8
, which is the latest version of the .NET Framework, which Microsoft continues to support as long as it runs on a supported Windows OS. This migration will not involve any major rewrite or modernization of the application such as moving to .NET Core or .NET 6+ and only minimal code changes will be made to ensure compatibility with Azure hosting requirements
.
Business Process Changes
Existing workflows and business logic will remain unchanged during this migration phase. The focus is on infrastructure transition rather than altering business operations.
SharePoint Online Enhancements
The current integration with SharePoint Online will remain as-is, with no redesign or enhancement of SharePoint functionality included in this scope.
Third-Party Integrations
Any integrations 
with external systems 
beyond 
the 
current scope are excluded
 from this migration effort. The focus remains on existing functionality and dependencies
.
Performance Optimization
No major performance tuning or re-architecture will be undertaken beyond the basic 
refac
toring
 approach. Optimization efforts are outside the scope of this phase.
Design Overview
Delivery Approach
Discovery
 
- Plan &amp; Build
During this phase, we focus
 on understanding the current 
environment
 and planning 
the 
migration.
 We gather details of the existing architecture, including applications, databases, and integrations, and identify key dependencies such as SSIS, Access databases, and SharePoint Online. Business requirements and compliance needs are also captured. The outputs of this phase include an
 AS-IS architecture document, 
a 
migration readiness assessment, and 
a 
risk
 and 
gap analysis.
Review
 - Assure &amp; Accept
During this phase, the proposed target architecture is validated with stakeholders, and reviews of the network security, data, and DevOps architectures are conducted to ensure alignment with governance and cost management policies. The primary outputs of this stage include an approved High-Level
 
Design, a finalized scope and migration plan, and formal signoff provided by the architecture and security teams
.
Implementation
 - Cutover &amp; Stabilise
During this phase, the migration is executed and the stability of the environment is ensured. The Azure landing zone is established, the agreed upon PaaS services for the application are deployed, and the databases are migrated to Azure SQL. Security controls including Key Vault, RBAC, and private endpoint are implemented, and monitoring capabilities are configured using App Insights, Log Analytics, and Sentinel. The key outputs of this phase include a fully deployed target architecture, operational runbooks and monitoring dashboards, and a complete handover to the support team
.
Impact Assessment
Business Impact
Automated data synchronization from TSE to BSE improves data availability by reducing manual intervention and delays. Hosting the web application on Azure enhances performance and accessibility, while Entra ID authentication and Azure security controls ensure compliance with organizational standards.
Risk:
 Potential business disruption during migration.
Mitigation:
 
A phased 
migration approach with parallel 
runs will be adopted, and a
 rollback plan to 
the 
on-prem environment 
will remain in place 
until cutover is validated.
Technical Impact
 
Th
is
 migration modernizes infrastructure by moving from on-prem IIS and SQL Server to Azure App Service and Azure SQL. Networking will shift to a Hub-Spoke architecture with VNet peering and private endpoints, and authentication will transition from Windows Authentication to Entra ID (
SAML 2.0
).
Risk:
 Legacy ASP.NET 
4
.0 compatibility issues on Azure App Service.
Mitigation:
 
A
n upgrade path to .NET
 Framework
 4.8 will be planned for the next phase, along with updating assembly references to support NuGet packages
.
Security Impact
  
Security will be strengthened through Azure WAF / App Gateway, SAML 2.0 SSO, Private DNS, Private endpoints, and Key Vault, NSGs reducing the attack surface. Centralized monitoring with Azure Sentinel 
and Defender 
for Cloud will enable proactive threat detection.

Architecture Design
System
 
A
rchitecture
Overview
This system adopts a hub
-
and
-
spoke network architecture, providing a secure, scalable, and 
well segmented
 environment. The Hub VNet contains centralized security services, including an Application Firewall that acts as the controlled entry point for all user traffic. This ensures every request is inspected using 
threat protection
 and filtering policies before being routed to the application layer. The BSE application is hosted in a dedicated Spoke VNet, alongside supporting services such as App Insights, Key Vault, Entra ID, and NSG rules that enforce 
subnet level
 protection. This separation allows the application to operate securely while maintaining private access to backend dependencies. A second Spoke VNet hosts the BSE SQL database, accessible only via private IPs and private endpoints. This strict isolation between application and data tiers enhances security, prevents exposure to the public internet, and ensures controlled 
east west
 traffic. Azure Data Factory integrates through 
express route
 networking to synchronize data from TSE to BSE using scheduled pipelines. By automating secure data movement within the private network, ADF ensures reliability and consistency without compromising isolation. Overall, the pattern strengthens security, governance, and maintainability by centralizing inspection and isolating workloads while still allowing efficient, controlled communication between components.
Figure 
1 – 
System architecture
Overvie
w
The proposed architecture adopts a Hub-Spoke model to enhance security, scalability, and operational efficiency while ensuring seamless integration between application and data layers.
 We have expl
ained 
the components in 
detail
 
below
.
Step 1 –
 
Identity, Access, and Secure Traffic Entry
The first step of the BSE architecture establishes secure and authenticated access to the web application and backend services using Microsoft Entra ID (DEFRA SAML 2.0), CCoE
managed Application Gateway, and Azure Private DNS Zones. All internal user roles
 
authenticate through Entra ID SAML 2.0 SSO, which provides a unified and centrally
governed identity control plane.
Once authenticated, traffic from all users passes through the CCoE Managed Application Gateway configured with 
Azure 
WAF, all inbound traffic reaches BSE via internal networks only, eliminating any dependency on public endpoints.
Name resolution is handled exclusively through Azure Private DNS Zones, aligned to the 
DTZ. Local
 namespace used across DEFRA workloads. This ensures that all internal resources, including BSE Web App, SQL private endpoints, ADF private endpoints, and Key Vault, are resolved privately
.
Private DNS
: 
 
Azure Private DNS Zones provide an isolated namespace used to resolve FQDNs for private Azure resources, including 
BSE
 PaaS services. Within this model, DTZ. Local, the CCoE
-
managed domain, is used as the underlying private domain. By default, DTZ. Local forwards all DNS queries to Azure DNS (preferable with CIDR 168.63.129.16), enabling seamless resolution of Azure-hosted services. To support hybrid operations, conditional forwarders are configured so that any requests to resolve non
-
Azure domains are automatically 
sent
 to Infoblox, maintaining enterprise-wide DNS governance. 
Throughout the lifecycle, DNS records are created, updated, and retired as resources evolve, ensuring reliable and automated name resolution without manual intervention
managed domain. By default, 
Azure domains are automatically 
routed
 to Infoblox, maintaining enterprise-wide DNS governance.
Azure WAF
:  
In the CCoE Application Gateway pattern, the Web Application Firewall (WAF) is a mandatory security capability built into Azure Application Gateway that protects internal web applications from common web
‑
based attacks. The WAF inspects all incoming HTTP(S) traffic and blocks threats such as SQL injection, cross
‑
site scripting (XSS), CSRF, and other OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities by applying Microsoft
‑
managed rule sets and real
‑
time threat intelligence. It acts as a security enforcement layer in front of backend services, ensuring harmful requests never reach the applications. The CCoE requires all gateways to operate using the WAF V2 tier, with policies created, enabled, monitored, and tuned centrally. Any custom rule changes must be reviewed and approved by CCoE Architecture and Security teams to ensure the organisation’s security posture is not compromised.
Application Gateway
:
  
Azure Application Gateway is a Layer 7 (HTTP
(
S
)
) load balancer that securely manages and routes web traffic to backend applications. It uses intelligent routing based on hostnames, URLs, query strings, 
while
 also enforcing Web Application Firewall (WAF) protection against OWASP Top 10 threats. It supports private, internal only access, end to end TLS encryption, autoscaling, custom routing rules, URL rewriting, and health probes to ensure backend reliability.
The CCoE defines Azure Application Gateway as a centrally approved, controlled, and managed pattern for securely exposing internal DEFRA applications. The CCoE mandates use of WAF V2 only, private IP
‑
only deployments, enforced TLS policies, Azure Policy compliance, and centralised diagnostics. Deployment and ongoing management are handled exclusively by the CCoE WebOps team using Infrastructure
‑
as
‑
Code; project teams cannot deploy their own gateways. Projects instead onboard their applications onto CCoE
‑
managed shared gateways, following strict routing, WAF, DNS, and security guidelines defined in the pattern.
Identity and Access
:
Authentication and protocols
OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) are used for authentication and authorisation.
Azure Entra ID issues JWT tokens for authenticated users and workloads.
Single Sign
On (SSO) is enabled for users.
Multi
Factor Authentication (MFA) is enforced using Conditional Access.
All access uses HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher.
Application and workload identities
The BSE web application is registered as an Azure Entra ID application.
Separate redirect URIs are configured for Dev, Test, Pre
Prod and Prod.
No secrets are stored in application code.
Azure Managed Identities are used for backend access, including: – App Service to
Azure SQL Database
App Service to Azure Key Vault
Azure Data Factory to Azure SQL and on
premises systems
Secrets and certificates are stored securely in Azure Key Vault.
Authorisation model
Access control is claims
based using information in JWT tokens.
Authorisation relies on group or role claims rather than individual user IDs.
No authorisation logic is hard
coded in the application.
All access assignments are managed centrally in Azure Entra ID.
Groups and roles
Azure Entra Security Groups represent business roles.
Groups are assigned to users, not individuals directly to applications.
User roles and administrative roles are clearly separated.
This enables consistent access control, simple joiner/leaver processes, and clear auditing.
Access controls by layer
Application layer access is enforced through Azure Entra ID and role
based logic.
Anonymous and shared accounts are not permitted.
Azure SQL uses Azure AD authentication only where possible.
Database permissions follow least
privilege (e.g. read
only access for analytics).
Direct database access is restricted to controlled environments 
Platform and infrastructure access is controlled using Azure RBAC.
Conditional Access
Conditional Access policies enforce MFA, approved locations, and compliant devices.
Legacy authentication protocols are blocked.
Production environment policies are more restrictive than non
production.
Break
glass (emergency access)
Two dedicated break
glass accounts are maintained in Azure Entra ID.
Accounts are cloud
only and excluded from Conditional Access by design.
Strong passwords are stored securely offline.
All usage is logged, monitored, and alerted.
Use is limited to formal incident scenarios with mandatory post
incident review.
Entra ID (DEFRA SSO SAML 2.0):
 
The Entra ID within DEFRA begins with identity creation and synchronisation, where users, groups, and attributes are sourced from on
‑
prem Active Directory to ensure consistent authentication and policy inheritance, with only cloud
‑
admin and third
‑
party identities created directly in Entra.
 
Authentication then occurs through DEFRA 
single sign
on
 
using SAML 2.0, with 
MFA
, and legacy
‑
authentication blocking enforced across all users.
Authorisation follows a strict group
‑
based model
 
roles are assigned only to groups, not individuals
 
ensuring least privilege, controlled access, and CCoE approval for any custom role creation. Conditional Access and governance policies continuously enforce device compliance, MFA requirements, and access restrictions, while all sign
‑
in, audit, and Conditional Access logs are collected and monitored through SOC
‑
integrated Log Analytics.
Finally, ongoing operations include privileged access monitoring, periodic entitlement reviews, timely removal of unnecessary access and continuous compliance checks to ensure the identity environment remains secure and aligned with DEFRA standards.

s:

ne operational area

mentioned above along with

Step
 
2 – Internal Traffic flow and Security
 (Hub VNET)
All BSE system traffic is routed through the centrally governed Hub VNet, where DEFRA’s network security controls are consistently applied. The Hub VNet hosts essential shared services including Azure Firewall, the Private DNS Resolver, and routing infrastructure that ensures all inbound and outbound flows are inspected, policy
‑
enforced, and logged.
The Azure Firewall provides a unified egress filtering and threat detection layer. All outbound traffic from the BSE application subnet flows through the firewall, ensuring that only approved destinations and ports are allowed. Logging from the firewall is streamed into a central Log Analytics workspace for SOC visibility.
Traffic entering the BSE Spoke VNet from the Hub is governed by VNet Peering, allowing secure low
‑
latency communication without transiting the public Internet. The Private DNS Resolver ensures that all name lookups in the BSE environment remain private, eliminating reliance on public DNS systems.
This step enforces Zero Trust principles by verifying every hop, restricting lateral movement, and maintaining a centralised security perimeter aligned with DEFRA’s Cloud Centre of Excellence guidelines
.
Step 3 - 
Application 
Components
 
(Spoke
 
Subnet)
The BSE Web Application runs inside a dedicated, isolated Application Subnet within the Spoke VNet. This tier is built on Azure App Service, which provides a fully managed runtime for .NET workloads with capabilities including autoscaling, managed patching, TLS termination, and seamless integration with Azure networking.
The application uses Regional VNet Integration for outbound connectivity and a Private Endpoint for inbound connectivity from the Application Gateway. Network access is enforced through NSGs placed on the subnet, restricting flows only to approved ports and resources such as SQL and Key Vault.
All application secrets and connection strings are stored securely in Azure Key Vault, accessed using Managed Identity, removing the need for hard
‑
coded credentials. Application Insights captures telemetry including performance metrics, request traces, availability tests, and end
‑
to
‑
end distributed logging.
This tier provides a secure, scalable, and centrally monitored runtime that supports all BSE user roles interacting with the web 
layer
.
App Service Networking:
Chosen Pattern
Multi-tenant Azure App Service with Private Link (Private Endpoint)
The application is hosted on Azure App Service (shared, multi-tenant PaaS).
Azure Private Link is used to expose the application privately inside the spoke VNet.
Service Environment (ASE / ILB) is not used.
Azure platform-enforced controls (not NSG/UDR)
App Service runtime isolation and tenant separation
TLS/HTTPS termination and certificate handling
Private Link service boundary enforcement
Platform-managed scaling, patching, and availability
Platform-level DDoS protection
Because the App Service is multi-tenant and not VNet-injected, NSGs and UDRs do not apply to the App Service runtime itself.
Customer-managed network controls (NSG / UDR / Firewall)
NSGs applied to spoke subnets
Private Endpoint subnet
Inbound restricted to Application Gateway
Default deny for other inbound traffic
App subnet
Allow only required outbound flows
UDRs applied to spoke subnets
Route all outbound traffic to the Hub firewall
Prevent direct internet egress
Hub firewall / NVA
Outbound traffic inspection and allow-listing
Controlled access to Azure Entra ID
Controlled access to Azure SQL via Private Endpoint
Controlled access to Key Vault, Storage, and monitoring endpoints
Controlled access to approved third-party APIs
Subnet Design and Delegation
App Service
App Service is not injected into the VNet
No subnet delegation is required
Private Endpoint Subnet
No subnet delegation
Network policies disabled for Private Endpoints
Protected by NSGs
L
inked via the Hub
Inbound Traffic Path
User accesses the application over HTTPS
Traffic enters via Application Gateway (WAF v2) in the Hub VNet
TLS termination and WAF inspection occur at Application Gateway
Application Gateway forwards traffic to the App Service Private Endpoint
Private Link delivers traffic over the Microsoft backbone to the App Service
There is no direct public access to the App Service
Outbound Traffic Routing
Spoke subnet UDRs route outbound traffic to the Hub firewall
The firewall enforces default-deny outbound access
Explicit allow rules are defined for required destinations
Private Endpoints are used for Azure SQL, Key Vault, and other supported services
Direct outbound internet access is not permitted

Step 4 – 
Database Tier (SQL + Private Endpoint + ADF Integration)
The BSE system uses an Azure SQL Database deployed in the Data Subnet of the Spoke. This database holds all operational BSE data, including case records, laboratory information, workflow actions, and reporting outputs. The database is deployed using the Serverless compute tier, which allows it to scale dynamically while optimising cost.
Connectivity is enforced through a Private Endpoint, ensuring that database access is entirely private and limited to App Service, ADF private endpoints, and authorised AVD
based SQL sessions. The database benefits from encryption at rest (TDE), encryption in transit (TLS), and zone
redundant storage for backups in Production.
Integration with ADF
Azure Data Factory plays a significant role in BSE for:
Scheduled ingestion from external TSE SQL systems
Data transformation and cleansing
Periodic data synchronisation into BSE SQL
Feeding models or analytics used by DEFRA AI, Wales, and Scotland teams
ADF connects using 
Managed Identity
 and 
Private Endpoints
, ensuring secure and private data movement.

Step 5 – 
AVD Direct Access to SQL (Read
‑
Only)
Data Analytics users connects
 Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) for secure, read
only access to the SQL database by specific analytical and operational roles.
Users such as Data Scientists, and SSMS
based support engineers access the BSE SQL database only through AVD. This prevents data exfiltration risks and ensures all access is fully audited.
Within AVD, users are presented with a controlled desktop containing:
SSMS
Analytical tools
Restricted network access
Conditional Access policies
Mandatory MFA
All SQL connectivity from AVD occurs through the SQL Private Endpoint, ensuring consistency with Zero Trust principles. SQL permissions enforce strictly read
only access, except for DBAs or authorised maintenance engineers when approved via PIM.
This design ensures the database remains secure while still supporting advanced analytics and operational investigation.
Data Architecture
Overview
The database architecture is designed to support the migration of the 
BSE
 
database
 from an 
on
-
premises
 SQL Server environment into Azure SQL Database. The target architecture leverages Azure’s managed database capabilities to deliver improved reliability, security, and operational efficiency while maintaining compatibility with existing application components. All existing tables, schemas, and relationships are preserved during migration, ensuring functional continuity, while the underlying platform benefits from Azure’s 
built
-
in performance tuning, automated backups, and high availability features
.
In the Azure environment, the database is hosted as a fully managed Azure SQL Database instance, eliminating the need for on
premises server maintenance and providing elastic compute scalability for varying workloads. Security is strengthened through Azure 
Entra ID
 authentication, role-based access control, encryption in transit and at rest via Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), and centralized auditing integrated with Azure Monitor. Network protection is enforced using private endpoints and firewall rules, ensuring the database is only accessible to approved application services and administrative identities.
Please refer the attached file and following image for data model architecture.

 – 
Data Architecture

Security Controls
Authentication:
 
The system uses 
Azure
 Entra ID
 to sign in users and 
manage identities
 for apps and services
 in all environments
. Regular SQL logins are turned off unless they’re absolutely needed.
Data Protection:
In transit: 
Data in transit is protected by enforcing TLS 1.2
/1.3
, ensuring all connections to the database are encrypted.
At rest
:
 
Data at rest is protected using Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), which is enabled by default. For enhanced control, a customer
managed key stored in Azure Key Vault can also be used.
Row-Level and Column-Level Security
:  
Row-level and column-level security can be applied as needed. Options include using row-level security to restrict access by user area, dynamic data masking to protect sensitive information, and Always Encrypted for safeguarding PII when required.
Backup: 
Database backups will be configured with environment
specific retention policies to support both operational recovery and security requirements. Backup retention will be set to 35 days for Production, 30 days for 
PreProd
, 14 days for Test, and 7 days for Development.
High availability &amp; disaster recovery: 
Production benefits from 
Zone
 redundancy through an auto
failover group, with DR disabled in Dev/Test and available as an optional configuration in Pre
Prod.
Auditing and Monitoring
Azure SQL auditing and monitoring are implemented to ensure security, compliance, and operational visibility across the database platform. 
Microsoft Defender for SQL is enabled to provide advanced threat protection, continuously monitoring for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and behavioural anomalies.
Audit logs are retained according to compliance requirements, typically ranging from 
180
 days to one year, ensuring historical traceability and supporting internal and external audit processes.
A
ccess Layer
The 
Azure application
 connects to Azure SQL Database using a Managed Identity, allowing it to authenticate without storing any passwords or credentials in code. The connection string (without secrets) is kept in application settings, while any sensitive configuration values are stored securely in Azure Key Vault
.
Database administrators
 sign in using Azure
 Entra ID
 groups, ensuring consistent and secure access control. Any temporary or elevated permissions are granted through Privileged Identity Management (PIM), which provides time limited, audited access for higher level tasks.
Business users 
connect through SQL
 Server Management Studio (SSMS)
 and 
sign in using Azure
 Entra ID
 groups
.
Integration access
: 
Azure Data Factory connects to the Azure SQL Database using a Managed Identity, which enables secure, password
 
less authentication without storing credentials in configuration files or code. A Linked Service is configured in Azure Data Factory to establish this connection, granting the managed identity the required database permissions.
Integration Layer
: 
The integration layer consists of two Azure Data Factory Data Flows responsible for orchestrating data integration activities. These Data Flows are executed through an Azure Data Factory pipeline, which manages their scheduling, dependencies, and overall execution flow
.
Data Flows
Data flow: TSE to BSE
This data flow handles ingestion from the TSE source system into the BSE environment. Azure Data Factory establishes a secure connection to the TSE database, extracts the required datasets, applies the necessary transformation logic, and loads the curated output into the 
dbo.BSESSImport
 table within the BSE database. This process ensures a consistent and automated transfer of source data into the BSE staging layer.

Monitoring and Alerting
:
 
Azure Data Factory Monitor is used to track pipeline, activity, and data flow execution status.
 Alerts are configured via Azure Monitor to notify support teams in the event of failures, prolonged runtimes, or repeated retry attempts.
 
Execution logs and run history are retained to support audit, troubleshooting, and reporting requirements.
Failure Handling and Rerun: 
Azure Data Factory pipelines are designed with built
‑
in retry policies for transient failures (for example, temporary connectivity issues
).
 
Permanent failures 
(e.g. schema changes, data type mismatches, invalid source data)
 
require manual investigation and resolution before rerunning the pipeline.
SLAs
: 
BSE
 
Data pipelines are expected to complete within scheduled window. Any 
0
failures impacting these SLAs are managed under the Tier 3 application support model, with a 4
‑
hour Recovery Time Objective (RTO).
Data Reconciliation &amp; Validation
Data reconciliation is performed after pipeline execution to ensure data completeness and accuracy following migration from SSIS to ADF.
Reconciliation checks include:
Pipeline execution status
Data validation 
will be carried out 
between 
the 
on
‑
premises 
database 
and 
the 
new destination database
 to ensure expected data patterns and outcomes. As the on
‑
premises data may be up to a day old, validation will focus on consistency checks such as data volumes and distribution trends rather than exact record
‑
level matching
.
Record count validation between source (TSE or BSE core tables) and target tables (BSESSImport and export tables).
Key column validation using defined business keys (e.g. AnimalID, TestingGroupID, ResultID).
Spot checks on critical business attributes to confirm correctness of transformation logic.
Reconciliation results will be 
documented 
capturing
 all
 the information 
outlined in the
 previous points.
Business
 Architecture
Overview
:
The business architecture 
describes
 how the BSE application operates within Defra’s cloud platform, 
connecting
 internal 
APHA 
users, cloud
hosted application components
, and 
the 
external 
TSE 
surveillance 
system. The architecture emphasises secure user authentication, efficient case and farm data management, structured integration with the external TSE database, and centralised document handling.
At the core of the architecture is the BSE Portal, which acts as the primary interface for all operational users. This portal is supported by the BSE Database, which stores case, farm, batch, and lookup information. Data from the external TSE surveillance system is periodically imported using Azure Data Factory, enabling the BSE Portal to display validated, up
to
date information for comparison with existing BSE cases. Case
related documents are held securely in SharePoint Online and accessed by users directly from the portal, while specialist analytics teams may continue using an 
SSMS
 reporting tool connected to the BSE Database 
via AVD
 for internal reporting needs.
Overall, the business architecture ensures secure authentication, efficient operational workflows, validated external data ingestion, and centralised document access
 
providing a modern, scalable foundation for BSE case management and reporting within Defra.
 
 
Figure
 
3
 – 
Business Architecture
 
Internal APHA users access the BSE Portal through 
Microsoft Entra ID
, ensuring all authentication aligns with Defra’s modern identity and security standards. When users log in, their identities are validated through Defra’s SSO policies, which include strong authentication requirements and centralised identity lifecycle management. By using Entra ID, the system guarantees that only authorised users
 
such as BSE case officers, VLA staff, analysts, and administrative teams
 
can access the application. This centralised authentication approach simplifies access management, improves auditability, and ensures consistent enforcement of multi
factor authentication (MFA) and conditional access policies across the entire BSE user population.
The BSE Portal is the primary application interface where authorised staff perform operational tasks related to BSE case management. Users can create new case entries, update case details, view historical data, and manage associated farm, batch, and lookup information. The portal also supports processes that compare TSE surveillance data with existing BSE records, enabling users to verify whether new information aligns with or contradicts existing case details. This comparison capability helps case officers and analysts rapidly identify anomalies, validate incoming surveillance data, and maintain data accuracy across the system. The portal’s workflows streamline everyday operations and ensure that information is presented consistently and securely.
Azure Data Factory serves as the integration layer responsible for ingesting surveillance data from the external TSE SQL Database, which resides outside Defra’s cloud environment. ADF pipelines securely retrieve the required surveillance datasets and apply transformation logic that standardises, cleanses, and structures the data before it is processed further. This integration step ensures that the information from the TSE system is reliable, usable, and compliant with BSE’s required data formats. The ability to automatically and regularly import TSE surveillance data ensures BSE users always work with accurate and up
to
date information sourced from national surveillance systems.
Once Azure Data Factory completes extraction and transformation of TSE surveillance data, the cleaned and structured output is written directly into the BSE Database. This enables the BSE system to perform automated or manual comparisons between newly imported surveillance data and existing BSE case records. Storing TSE data within the BSE Database ensures data consistency, supports validation processes, and allows BSE officers to quickly detect mismatches or duplicates across surveillance and case datasets. This integrated data approach enhances operational accuracy and supports compliance with regulatory reporting obligations.
Specialist APHA data analytics users are given controlled, read
only access to the BSE Database, allowing them to perform internal analysis, reporting, and statistical assessments without affecting live operational data. This role is separate from standard BSE portal users and is designed for analysts or data teams who rely on structured data to generate insights. Their access is controlled to ensure data integrity while still enabling valuable data exploration and reporting activities. By supporting database
level access for analytics teams, the architecture ensures operational staff, analysts, and surveillance experts can collaborate effectively while maintaining strong data governance.
Case
related documents
 
including reports, evidence, reference files, and attachments
 
are stored securely in SharePoint Online. Instead of storing documents inside the BSE Database or the portal itself, SharePoint acts as the central document repository. The BSE Portal generates secure hyperlinks that allow users to open or download documents stored in SharePoint. This approach aligns with Defra’s cloud collaboration strategy, ensures secure document access, maintains version control, and reduces storage costs in the application’s core databases. Users benefit from consistent access to all relevant case files directly from the BSE Portal interface.
DevOps Architecture
Overview
This DevOps architecture establishes a secure, automated pipeline for building and deploying applications across Azure environments. Development begins in feature branches, which trigger 
Continuous Integration (
CI
)
 processes upon pull requests. Azure Pipelines performs build, test, validation, and artifact publishing, while Azure Artifacts stores templates. 
Continuous Delivery (
CD
)
 pipelines then deliver these artifacts through gated, multi
stage environments using OIDC
 (OpenID Connect)
 service connections and secrets from Azure Key Vault. Deployments flow from the hub to spoke networks, provisioning app services, other PAAS services, SQL resources securely. Comprehensive monitoring and approval workflows ensure visibility, compliance, and reliable application delivery
.

 – 
DevOps Architecture

DevOps Deployment Stages
Network &amp; 
Security
Security Architecture
Overview:
This Azure hub
 - 
spoke security architecture establishes a tightly controlled, segmented environment where all traffic is routed through a central Hub containing Azure Firewall for perimeter protection, threat inspection, and unified egress control. Application workloads run in a dedicated Spoke
 subnet
 using private PaaS services, NSGs. The Data Spoke 
subnet
 hosts Azure SQL databases accessible only through Private Endpoints, ensuring full isolation and encrypted data flows. Centralised monitoring with Microsoft Sentinel and Log Analytics provides threat detection, visibility, and automated incident response across the entire estate
Figure
 
5
 – 
Security Architecture
Steps Explained
Step 1: 
Ingress Security &amp; Identity Protection
All user access to the application is routed through the CCoE
managed Application Gateway, which is protected by Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF
). This provides the solution’s controlled and secured ingress boundary. Incoming traffic is authenticated using
 
DEFRA SAML 2.0
 / Entra ID, 
ensuring only 
authorised users can reach application resources.
 
Private DNS and internal identity services further ensure that only internal, trusted users can resolve and access workloads within the 
BSE
 VNet
.
Step 
2
: 
Hub–Spoke Network Security
The 
BSE
 solution is deployed in a spoke VNet that is securely connected to the central hub via VNet peering. Traffic between the hub and spoke is tightly governed using NSGs attached to each spoke subnet, enforcing secure segmentation and preventing unauthorised lateral movement.
Step 
3
: 
Subnet
Level Segmentation
 
&amp; Zero
Trust Enforcement
Each subnet in the solution has a dedicated NSG, in line with DEFRA’s requirement that all subnets 
must
 be associated with an NSG. 
The mandatory deny
all (priority 4096) NSG rule applies at the subnet level, meaning all resources within the spoke VNet subnets operate under a zero
trust model.
Only explicitly defined communication between application components is permitted.
All connectivity between App Service, Key Vault, SQL Database, and other components is controlled via specific custom allow rules.
Step 
4
: PaaS 
&amp; Data 
Spoke Security
The Application Tier and Database Tier operate in securely segmented subnets under strict Zero
Trust controls. The 
BSE Web App
 runs within a dedicated App Service Plan integrated with the VNet using 
Regional VNet Integration
. All inbound traffic reaches the Web App through a 
Private Endpoint
, meaning the application is never exposed to public networks. NSGs restrict the App Service’s outbound traffic to the Hub Firewall and authorised Azure services via service tags only.
The 
BSE SQL Database
 resides in a separate data subnet, connected exclusively through a 
SQL Private Endpoint
. This ensures that the SQL service can only be reached by:
BSE Web App
Azure Data Factory Managed Private Endpoints
Azure Virtual Desktop sessions used by analytics teams
SQL firewall rules enforce “deny public network access,” ensuring 100% data
plane isolation. The database benefits from encryption at rest (TDE), encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), strict RBAC, Defender for SQL, vulnerability scanning, and anomaly detection. Zone
redundant backups (ZRS) ensure resilience in production.
Key Vault secures connection strings, secrets, and certificates, accessed exclusively via managed identities. Defender for Key Vault adds behavioural monitoring to detect unusual access patterns.
This layered model ensures the application and database tiers remain fully private, strictly controlled, and protected from unauthorised access
.
Step 
5
: 
AVD &amp; Analytics Security Controls (Read
‑
Only SQL Access)
The BSE architecture includes a dedicated security pathway for analytics staff who require direct database insights while maintaining strict governance. 
Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD)
 provides a secure, isolated environment through which internal analytics users access SQL Server using SSMS in 
read
only mode
.
AVD sessions run in a locked
down environment controlled by Conditional Access, MFA, session logging, device compliance, and NSGs that permit only SQL Private Endpoint access. This ensures analysts cannot bypass application logic or connect directly from unmanaged endpoints.
All SQL access via AVD is monitored and securely logged, providing a fully auditable trail and ensuring compliance with data governance, forensic requirements, and security policies.
DB Access Governance
Direct user access to the production Azure SQL Database using SSMS is permitted only from an Azure
‑
hosted Virtual Desktop.
 
No direct connectivity from on
‑
premises devices or the public internet is allowed.
Read
‑
Only Access
Users are assigned read
‑
only database roles. Write, update, and delete permissions are explicitly denied at the database level
 
to prevent any data modification
.
 
Where applicable, access may be provided through a read
‑
only replica to further isolate production workloads. Any requirement for elevated access follows a formal approval process, with role assignments, permission configurations, and approval records retained to evidence compliance
.
Network and Firewall Restrictions
Connectivity to the production Azure SQL Database is tightly controlled through network and firewall rules
 (defined 
under 3.1 Network Security
)
. Access is permitted only from the approved Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) subnet and f
or
 authorised 
users only
. Public network access is disabled or heavily restricted, ensuring that users cannot connect directly from on
‑
premises or external networks. Firewall configurations, subnet definitions, and access rules are maintained as evidence of enforced network isolation.
Privileged Access Management (PIM / JIT)
Any privileged or administrative database access is governed through Azure Entra ID Privileged Identity Management (PIM). Elevated access is granted on a just
‑
in
‑
time, approval
‑
based, and time
‑
limited basis, ensuring that standing privileged access is avoided. All elevation requests, approvals, activation durations, and role assignments are logged and retained, providing a clear audit trail of privileged access usage.
Auditing, Monitoring, and Review
Database auditing and diagnostic logging are enabled and integrated with Azure Monitor to capture login activity, query execution, and failed access attempts. Alerts are configured to detect anomalous or suspicious query behaviour. Audit logs, alert configurations, monitoring dashboards, and access review outcomes collectively provide evidence that database access is continuously monitored and governed.

These services provide continuous monitoring, threat intelligence, vulnerability management and behavioural analytics.

Solution Sec
urity 
Setup
Network Security
Application Firewall
The Application Firewall acts as the first line of defence, inspecting all inbound traffic before it reaches application resources. It applies Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules to block malicious access patterns and enforce security policies, ensuring only legitimate requests are processed.
VNET Peering (Between Hub–Spokes)
Secure VNET peering connects the hub and spoke networks, enabling private, low-latency communication between components. This configuration ensures that traffic remains within the Azure backbone, eliminating any need for public exposure and reducing security risks.
Network Security Groups (NSGs)
NSGs are applied at the subnet level within the spoke networks to enforce strict inbound and outbound traffic rules. They segment workloads and control communication between services, providing an additional layer of security and governance.
Based on CCoE guidance
 and 
Microsoft 
design patterns, App Tier subnets commonly use

hosted, so no dedicated /24 AGW subnet is needed.
 A /23 VNet (512 IPs) provides sufficient capacity 
for all required subnets and Private Endpoints 
without over
allocating address space.

Firewall Security Rules
Ingress Path
 
The ingress path allows HTTPS-only traffic from the internet into the hub via App Gateway/WAF or Firewall, where WAF policies provide first-layer protection.
 Traffic is then routed from the hub into the application subnet through NSG rules that also permit App Gateway health probes.
Finally, the application reaches Entra ID endpoints for login redirection and token validation, completing the secure authentication flow.

The egress path allows the application to securely reach required services such as Azure SQL, on

third 
party APIs are permitted but restricted via the firewall using FQDN-based rules. All general internet access is blocked, ensuring only explicitly authorised destinations are reachable. This enforces strong outbound governance and minimises unnecessary exposure.

NSG Data Subnet
 
The Data Subnet NSG allows only controlled inbound SQL access from the App Subnet, ensuring the database is reachable only from trusted application tiers. All other inbound traffic is denied by default, while outbound traffic is force tunnelled through the hub firewall with direct internet egress blocked. This enforces a tightly secured, isolated data layer with strictly governed connectivity.

Service
 
Resilience
 
Resilience in the proposed Azure-based BSE architecture ensures continuous service availability, fault tolerance, and rapid recovery from failures. Key components like Azure Entra ID, DNS, Virtual Networks, App Service (Premium tier), Azure SQL Database, and Data Factory are designed with multi-zone deployments, geo-redundancy, and automated failover mechanisms. High availability is achieved through load balancing, autoscaling, and zone redundancy, while disaster recovery leverages paired-region replication, Azure Site Recovery, and geo-replicated databases. Security and governance are enforced via DEFRA CCoE guidelines, including identity hardening, private endpoints, and immutable backups. Regular monitoring, DR drills, and compliance guardrails ensure operational continuity and compliance.
Summary
Components
Resilience Factors
Azure App Service (Premium Tier)
Resilience: Deploy App Service (Premium v3) with Zone
 
redundant plan where available; enable Auto scale (instances) and Always On; use Deployment Slots for safe rollouts/quick rollback; connect via private endpoints; cache dependencies.
DEFRA CCoE alignment: Standard PaaS pattern with private access, secrets in Key Vault, CI/CD approvals, and operational monitoring to meet NCSC principles.
Azure Entra ID
Entra ID is globally distributed with redundant auth endpoints; use conditional access and break
glass accounts; enable Privileged Identity Management (PIM).
DEFRA CCoE alignment: Enforce least privilege, strong auth (MFA), role separation, and auditable elevation to meet NCSC Principles on identity, authentication, and governance.
DNS
Use Azure DNS with health
probe driven endpoints; implement Traffic Manager or Front Door for global DNS
based routing and endpoint health checks.
DEFRA CCoE alignment: Centralised routing standards and service health monitoring under governance; change management via approvals. 
Virtual Network (Hub
Spoke), VNet Peering &amp; NSG
Hub
spoke with Azure Firewall/Firewall Premium in hub; redundant VNet peering
 
NSGs with deny
by
default; use Service Tags and Application Security Groups; enable Network Watcher/Connection Monitor.
DEFRA CCoE alignment: Standardised network patterns, central firewalling, policy enforcement via Azure Policy/Blueprints to meet NCSC network segregation and protective monitoring
 Azure SQL Database 
Choose Business Critical (or Premium) with Zone Redundancy; enable connection retries in clients; use private endpoints; monitor with SQL Insights.
DEFRA CCoE alignment: Data classification, encryption at rest/in transit, private access only
 
meeting NCSC data protection principles.
Azure Data Factory
Use Managed Azure Integration Runtime (Azure IR) where possible, as it provides built
in high availability and zone
redundant execution. When Self
Hosted IR is required, deploy a minimum of 3 nodes across availability zones or subnets, enable per
activity 
to 
retry and timeout logic, and configure pipeline
level alerts with custom error
handling patterns. When using Managed Private Endpoints, ensure DNS resolution is correctly configured and the Private Endpoint subnet is adequately sized
.
 
Table 
27
 – 
Resilience Plan
4.2 
High Availability
Azure SQL
Azure SQL Database provides high availability through its Always On architecture, which maintains multiple internal replicas to ensure continuous uptime. When configured as zone
‑
redundant, these replicas are distributed across different availability zones, enabling the platform to automatically fail over between replicas without user impact.
Application Layer
The application layer benefits from Azure’s resilient networking foundation, where the central Application Firewall in the hub VNet can be deployed across zones for increased availability. Additionally, VNet peering, Private DNS, and NSGs are inherently redundant services, ensuring uninterrupted connectivity and secure communication even during component
‑
level failures.
Disaster Recovery
Regional DR
The disaster recovery design includes cross
‑
region SQL replication using Data Sync or, where suitable, auto
‑
failover groups for production deployments. This includes provisioning a secondary SQL server in a paired region, replicating the VNet, private DNS zones, and firewall rules to maintain operational continuity. Runbooks and automation scripts form part of the DR approach to streamline recovery activities.
The solution uses 
zone
redundant 
in the primary region and a 
paired
region DR model
 aligned with Defra and CCoE guidance. Critical services such as App Service, SQL, and Key Vault are replicated or pre
provisioned in the secondary region. Azure SQL Failover Groups provide 
RPO of minutes
 and data continuity. Network, private endpoints, and DNS are mirrored for seamless regional recovery.
Failover Planning
Failover can be 
automatic
 through auto
-
failover groups or manually 
controlled
 using runbooks for Data Sync environments. 
The plan also includes DNS cutover and application connection redirection to maintain service continuity during failover events.
 
F
ailover is managed through 
global traffic routing
 to shift users to the secondary region when the primary becomes unavailable. Zone
redundant components ensure local continuity, while regional failover activates pre
provisioned App Service, Key Vault, and SQL via the failover group. This approach supports 
RTO of 
8-48
 hours
, depending on automation and service tier
.
Backup and Restore
Automated Backups
Azure SQL provides 
fully 
automated 
backup capabilities to ensure data protection and recovery. The system performs weekly 
full backups
, daily
 differential backups, and transaction log backups every 
5
 - 
10 
minutes
. All backups are
 stored in 
ZRS
-
redundant storage
 for high durability and disaster resilience.
Point-in-Time Restore
Databases can be restored to any point within 
the configured 
retention 
period, which ranges from 
7 to 35 days
. This feature enables quick
 recovery from accidental 
data loss
 or corruption
 without impacting overall service availability.
Retention 
Period:
Database b
ackup retention will be set to 35 days for Production, 30 days for PreProd, 14 days for Test, and 7 days for Development.
 
Application data within the database 
has no archival process and will be retained 
for extended periods
 
supporting compliance, 
and 
audit requirements
.
Data Sync
 Recovery
In the event of a failure, the sync
 metadata database can be restored, and sync agents reattached to resume 
operations. Detailed runbooks guide administrators through the recovery process to ensure 
synchronization 
continuity
.
Management and Monitoring
Overview 
The 
BSE
 platform relies on Azure Monitor and CCoE
mandated monitoring services to provide observability, security visibility, performance tracking, and operational insights across the solution.
 
Azure Monitor is the primary telemetry ingestion and analysis service, used to collect, analyse, and act on telemetry from the App Service, private SQL database, networking components, and integrated security services such as Defender and Azure Sentinel.
 A
lthough Logic Monitor is CCoE’s strategic operational monitoring tool, Azure Monitor (and its sub
components, such as Application Insights, Metrics, Workbooks, and Dashboards) is approved for foundation service deployments in Defra Azure environments.
Azure Monitor
Azure Monitor is allowed in CCoE
managed environments but is not the main monitoring tool. All log data must be sent to the central CCoE Log Analytics workspace, and only CCoE
approved Azure Monitor features may be used, with any additional needs requiring review. Configurations must follow strict security standards such as TLS 1.2, conditional access, and least
privilege permissions. These controls ensure Azure Monitor remains secure, compliant, and consistent across Defra environments.
Logic
 
Monitor
 
Logic
 
Monitor is the main operational monitoring tool, giving central visibility of infrastructure, availability, alerts, and daily operations. While Azure Monitor provides useful platform and application insights, Logic
 
Monitor is used for real
time monitoring and incident detection, so monitoring designs should prioritise its integration. Azure logs and telemetry must still be sent to the central Log Analytics workspace for SOC/SIEM needs. This approach keeps monitoring consistent and aligned with CCoE’s operational strategy across all Defra cloud services.

Migration
 
Data Migration Approach
Overview
: This section describes the strategy for migrating on
-
premises SQL Server databases to 
Azure SQL Database 
within the
 DEFRA Azure Cloud
. The approach ensures data integrity, security, minimal downtime, and continuity of service for applications and end users. 
Database t
o migrate: 
DEFACPVWPSQL001
\
 BSE
Figure 6
 – 
Data Migration Approach
Migration m
ethod and Tools
The migration will use 
Microsoft-supported Azure utilities
.
Azure Migrate- Discovery and assessment:
 Azure Migrate is a service that helps you decide on, plan, and execute your migration to Azure. An assessment with the Discovery and assessment tool is a point in time snapshot of data and measures the readiness and estimates the effect of migrating on-premises servers to Azure.
Azure Database Migration Service:
 is a tool that helps you simplify, guide, and automate your database migration to Azure.
Pre-Migration validation
/
 
Database Assessment/
Azure Migrate, together with the Azure Migrate Appliance, will be used to assess a copy of the live on
‑
premises database. This ensures that the production database is not impacted during discovery or analysis. The assessment provides a point
‑
in
‑
time evaluation of the database’s readiness for migration to Azure SQL, identifying compatibility issues, unsupported features, required schema changes, and potential migration blockers before the migration is initiated.
Cut
over Steps
Complete schema migration to Azure SQL using DMS (Schema Only mode).
Perform full data migration using DMS.
Validate successful completion of data load.
Execute functional and performance testing.
Freeze source database for final cutover (if offline mode is selected).
Redirect application connections to Azure SQL Database.
Post
‑
cutover verification and monitoring.
Downtime Window
Application will have no downtime during the database migration
 
because it’s independent 
parallel 
system which 
we will cut over 
only
 after 
validating the 
performance 
and accuracy of the migrated system
.
The exact duration 
of 
database 
migration
 will be confirmed after assessment results, dataset size, and performance testing outcomes are validated.
Rollback Strategy
The source on
‑
premises SQL Server database will remain unchanged and available until migration completion is confirmed.
In the event of any critical issues during or after cutover, the application will be switched back to the on
premises setup, reconnecting to the on
premises database. The Azure SQL Database will be isolated to allow detailed investigation and resolution of the issue.
Data Reconciliation
Row count comparison between source and target databases.
Spot checks on business
‑
critical tables.
Verification of stored procedures, views, and indexes.
Execution of representative queries and comparison of results.
 Queries will be defined in Low-level design document.
Acceptance Criteria
All schema objects are migrated without errors.
100% of required data is successfully migrated and reconciled.
Functional tests confirm application behaviour matches the source system.
Performance benchmarks meet or exceed agreed thresholds.
Security and access controls are correctly configured and validated.
Stakeholder sign
‑
off is obtained from business and technical teams.

document
 for detailed strategy

8 - 48 hours
 of data is lost, in alignment with Tier 3 service levels.

8 - 48 hours
 after a failure, as required under Tier 3 service levels.
